title: WHERE Clause
description: Learn how to use the WHERE clause to filter rows returned by a query based on search conditions.

data.text: The SELECT statement retrieves all rows from a table, but this is often unnecessary because the application may only need to process a subset of rows. To retrieve rows that satisfy one or more conditions, you use the WHERE clause in the SELECT statement.

data.title: WHERE Clause Syntax
data.content: The search_condition is a logical expression used to filter rows.
data.code:
SELECT
    select_list
FROM
    table_name
WHERE
    search_condition;

data.text: In this syntax, the search_condition is a logical expression or a combination of multiple logical expressions. In SQL, a logical expression is also known as a predicate.
In the WHERE clause, you specify a search condition to filter rows returned by the FROM clause. The WHERE clause only returns the rows for which the search_condition evaluates to TRUE.

data.title: Three-Valued Logic
data.text: SQL Server uses three-valued predicate logic where a logical expression can evaluate to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN. The WHERE clause will not return any row that causes the predicate to evaluate to FALSE or UNKNOWN.

data.title: Simple Equality Filter
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    category_id = 1
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Combining Conditions with AND
data.content: Find products in category 1 with model year 2018.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    category_id = 1 AND model_year = 2018
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Comparison Operators
data.content: Find products with list price greater than 300 and model year 2018.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price > 300 AND model_year = 2018
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Using OR Operator
data.content: Find products with list price greater than 3000 or model year 2018.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price > 3000 OR model_year = 2018
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Using BETWEEN Operator
data.content: Find products with list prices between 1899 and 1999.99.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price BETWEEN 1899.00 AND 1999.99
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Using IN Operator
data.content: Find products with list price of 299.99, 369.99, or 489.99.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    list_price IN (299.99, 369.99, 489.99)
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Using LIKE Operator
data.code:
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    category_id,
    model_year,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    product_name LIKE '%Cruiser%'
ORDER BY
    list_price;

data.title: Clause Processing Order
data.text: When the SELECT statement includes both WHERE and FROM clauses, SQL Server processes them in the following sequence: FROM, WHERE, and then SELECT.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use the WHERE clause to filter rows based on one or more conditions.
The search condition is a Boolean expression that evaluates to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN.
The WHERE clause only returns rows where the condition evaluates to TRUE.
Combine conditions with AND, OR, and parentheses for complex filtering.
SQL Server processes FROM before WHERE, then SELECT.
